title: The Educated Barbarian: Meditations analysis (part. 9)
summary: Part 9 of NH's reading of Marcus Aurelius's Meditations, beginning Book 5 in a freezing room. He covers getting out of bed, why rest has to be earned through work, and a list of Stoic virtues (sincerity, frugality, frankness, not blaming your body), and ends with doing good without expecting anything back.
claims: As a child NH was told on waking to count his limbs and be happy if they were all there, and to be grateful for a bed, a roof and food; he still tries to live by that
You were born with legs, not as a slug, so once you are done sleeping it is time to be active and productive
The never-rest, sleep-when-dead warrior attitude is stupid; rest is natural, but accepting rest as necessary means accepting work as equally necessary
A rest day is a rest from something; if you have not trained, it is not a rest day, you are just skipping
NH gets antsy if he rests several days in a row because he feels he has not earned it; rest is sweetest after work
Productivity is tied to self-worth; the laziest people tend to hate themselves, because you express who you are through action, not rest
Do not judge something on others' reports before applying your own mind to it, and accept criticism only if it is sound; unsound criticism has no power over you
Being dignified for NH means not being loud or an inconvenience in public; you should be seen, not heard
Stoicism is not masochism: you never seek pleasure for its own sake, but you do not reject it as a by-product; eat food because it is beneficial, and if it is also pleasurable, fine
Frugality and minimalism fit Stoicism; consumerism pulls you off the path and possessions are nice to have but ultimately worthless
Frankness is the hardest virtue to practise today because people would rather be strung along than told directly, but you should say what you mean
Hyperbole sits close to lying, and the more you stack it, the closer you get to a lie
Never blame your body: saying you have bad genetics means your parents gave you a bad body; your body is a vessel and it is not the vessel's fault if you are a poor captain
Restlessness usually means you are not working; once you work, restlessness goes away
Virtues are not innate but dormant; you grow them through exercise, and how fast depends on how much you want them
When people fish for compliments by saying they are terrible, NH agrees with them flatly, because someone has to call them out or they will stagnate
NH's personal policy: when he lends money he considers it gone, and he only lends to good friends he knows will repay; helping with an expectation of return is impure
Usury is condemned in many cultures because helping others for interest perverts something that should be about community
Do good actively whenever you can without expecting anything in return; remembering it only shows you that you can keep doing it
